sections.html: Magna is a Salt Lake County city on the west side of the valley, northeast of the Oquirrh Mountains and just south of the Great Salt Lake. The 2020 count was 29,251 people, up 10.4 percent from 26,505 in 2010, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 35,401. Single-family subdivisions went up south and east of the historic center in the 1970s. Those houses are now about fifty years old, so a seller may be weighing repairs to the roof, furnace or plumbing before listing.

sections.h2: From copper mill town to city
sections.html:
Magna began as a farming and ranching settlement, and pioneers started arriving in 1851. The turning point came in 1906, when the Utah Copper Company began building the Magna Mill. The name comes from the Latin word for great and was officially adopted on October 19, 1915. Older neighborhoods around Main Street went by names such as Greektown, Japantown, Snaketown and Little Italy.

Magna became a township in 2001 and a metro township in 2017. It became a city on May 1, 2024, under Utah House Bill 35.

A magnitude 5.7 earthquake hit at 7:09 a.m. on March 18, 2020, with its epicenter about 6 kilometers north-northeast of Magna. It was the strongest in Utah since the 1992 St. George quake. Nobody died and injuries were minor, but bricks fell from some buildings and about 145 historic structures were damaged. Cyprus High School took some of the worst damage. Building-related damage was put at about $62 million of $629 million in total losses.

If your house had quake repairs, keep the paperwork, since buyers ask what was fixed. A house with repairs still undone is one reason owners choose to sell as-is.

Copper mining drove the local economy for most of a century. Mills shut during the Great Depression and revived around 1940 with wartime demand, and Hercules Powder began producing rocket motors at its Bacchus Works plant south of town. Northrop Grumman now runs a solid rocket motor plant in Magna.

Kennecott Land's West Bench plan calls for major development, including an urban center along I-80. Main Street has seen commercial decline and some vacant storefronts, though it was remodeled in 2006 and is a popular filming location. Compare recent nearby sales and do not assume the West Bench plan will lift your price. Ask a local agent or a cash buyer what comparable houses actually sold for in the last few months, because that number matters more than any plan on paper.

West 3500 South (SR-171) is the main east and west road, and South 8400 West (SR-111) is the main north and south road. UTA route 35 runs along 3500 South every 15 minutes on weekdays and loops through Main Street, and the TRAX Green Line is nearby.

The Granite School District serves Magna. Elementary schools are Copper Hills, Elk Run, Lake Ridge, Magna and Pleasant Green. Matheson Junior High is the middle school, and Cyprus High School competes at the 5A level.

The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District, called the MSD, serves Magna along with Kearns, Copperton, White City, Emigration Canyon, Brighton and unincorporated Salt Lake County. It handles planning and zoning, building permits and inspections, code enforcement and business licensing. Police, fire and sanitation come from other providers, so call the right office for each issue, and keep a note of whom you spoke with.

Magna code violationWhat triggers it
WeedsTaller than six inches
Outdoor storageJunk left outside
ParkingOn dirt or grass
VehiclesMore than two unregistered or inoperable on a property
Unpermitted useSigns, home businesses or short-term rentals
OccupancyToo many unrelated occupants
SetbacksCarports too close to a property line

Construction without a permit goes to the MSD Building Department at (385) 468-6688. Code enforcement is at 860 W Levoy Drive, Suite 300, Taylorsville, phone (385) 910-5780. Call to confirm current rules for your address before you list.

Salt Lake County mails tax notices by November 1, and taxes are due November 30. Unpaid current-year taxes turn delinquent on December 1, and the penalty rises after January 31. The Auditor sends the tax sale listing on March 15, and the final tax sale takes place on the fourth Thursday of May.

Begin with a walk around the outside, since code enforcement here centers on exterior conditions. Cut weeds, clear stored junk, move vehicles onto a hard surface and make sure any carport sits clear of the property line. These small fixes keep a violation notice from landing in the middle of a sale.

Then look inside. If the house is from the 1970s, note the age of the roof, furnace and water heater. Gather receipts for any quake repairs and permits for finished basements or additions. Buyers and inspectors ask about all of these, and clear answers keep a deal from stalling.

If a repair list looks long, compare the cost of fixing against selling as-is, where the buyer takes the house in its current condition and you skip the work.
Unpaid taxes are paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the county for the balance and give it to the title officer so the payoff is clear before you sign.

The Salt Lake County Recorder is at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, Salt Lake City, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., phone 385-468-8145. The county's Property Watch service sends alerts to help protect a property, and the county posts a guide for handling property after an owner's death.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Magna
sections.html:
The sale ends with the same title company closing and recorded deed as any other, minus a lender's appraisal and underwriting. You share the address and condition, review the offer and sign a purchase contract.

  • Gather the deed or trust papers, and any code notices.
  • Ask the title company to confirm liens and taxes.
  • Pick a closing date that works around repairs or move-out plans.

Owners with quake repairs left undone, inherited houses or MSD code notices are among those who consider this path.

With no lender, there is no appraisal that can come in low and no bank repair list. You skip staging, photos and weeks of showings. The buyer takes the house in its current state, including an old furnace or a cracked chimney, and the title company handles the liens, taxes and recording. You keep control of the closing date, so you can line it up with a move or with the end of a repair project.

faqs.a: Yes. Magna became a city on May 1, 2024, under Utah House Bill 35. It had been a township from 2001 and a metro township from 2017.

faqs.q: How many people live in Magna?
faqs.a: The estimate is 35,401 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was 29,251.

faqs.q: Who handles code enforcement for a Magna house?
faqs.a: The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District. Call (385) 910-5780 for code enforcement or (385) 468-6688 for construction without a permit.

faqs.q: When are Salt Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the penalty increases after January 31.

faqs.q: Did the 2020 earthquake damage homes in Magna?
faqs.a: Some buildings were damaged. The magnitude 5.7 quake on March 18, 2020 had its epicenter about 6 kilometers north-northeast of Magna, and building-related damage was estimated at about $62 million.
